clue.text: Planets near suns developed without source of religious discord

indicators.note: developed means the letters of the three words are worked into a new shape
without tells us a letter must be dropped from the fodder before rearranging
the source of a word is its first letter, taken from religious

explanation.surface: An astronomy note on worlds forming near stars, oddly tied to quarrels over faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without source of religious' removes R (first letter of 'religious') from PLANETSNEARSUNS; 'developed' then rearranges the remaining fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad feeling and quarrelling between people is a state of strife, the sense of discord here.

clue.text: Grandma hugs upcoming fancy English composer

indicators.note: hugs means the grandma word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother

indicators.note: upcoming in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise, like fancy!

explanation.surface: A grandmother embraces an imaginative composer from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy!' and 'My!' are both cries of surprise; 'upcoming' reverses MY to YM in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Nyman is the English minimalist who scored The Piano.

clue.text: Fine soil mostly covering grassed Us railway in 23 's city

indicators.note: covering means the soil word goes around the other pieces
mostly means the soil word loses its final letter

parts.note: loess is a fine wind-blown silt soil
to grass is to inform on, so grassed means sang to the police
the El is the elevated railway in American cities such as Chicago

explanation.surface: Fine soil laid over grassy US railway lines in a film city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' and 'covering' build the city around a song to the police; 'Grassed' is British slang for informed on. 23 is TINSELTOWN, so its city is where Hollywood lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood lies within this Californian city, so Tinseltown is part of it.

clue.text: Major route from place set aside for creative endeavour?

definitions.text: place set aside for creative endeavour?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a main road leads from a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a made-up word built like 'eatery' or 'brewery': a place for art.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or channel of traffic is a trunk route; whimsically, an art-place on the pattern of eatery.

clue.text: One article with another constricting firm snake

parts.note: an is one form of the indefinite article

indicators.note: constricting means squeezing around, so the article group holds the firm word

parts.note: and means with or plus
co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a is another article

explanation.surface: A grammar note about articles squeezing a company, then a serpent appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constricting' puts CO inside ANANDA; the word also fits the snake, which kills by constricting.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American constrictor is one of the biggest serpents.

clue.text: Revealed temperature from an earlier period

parts.note: old means belonging to a time long past

explanation.surface: Disclosed what the temperature was in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose a secret is to have informed someone, so revealed and narrated share that sense.

clue.text: Failing God, live in sin

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the letters collapse into a new order

explanation.surface: Turning from God to live a life of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' rearranges GODLIVEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked conduct or wrongdoing is the same as sinning, used here as a noun.

clue.text: Isle's ten-hand strains, keeping work up?

definitions.text: Isle's ten-hand strains, keeping work up?

indicators.note: keeping means the anagram holds the other piece inside it
strains means the letters are stretched and twisted into a new order

parts.note: the word isle plus its s, all used as letters

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Breeds of small horse from an island, working hard to carry their load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strains' rearranges the island and ten-hand letters; 'up' turns the work word in this down clue and 'keeping' holds it. The whole clue also defines: small island breeds used for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hardy horses from a Scottish archipelago, often around ten hands tall and bred for work.

clue.text: Superficial online media son edited

indicators.note: edited means the letters are revised and rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a son's online media output is shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges ONLINEMEDIASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking depth, as a flat character with only one side, is shallow or superficial.

clue.text: New house back in French city

indicators.note: back tells us the word for a house is to be read in reverse

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a common British home type

explanation.surface: A new home somewhere in a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SEMI into IMES; a SEMI is a British semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nîmes is a city in southern France, famed for its Roman arena.

clue.text: Transport in scramble with reduced rail service: fancy catching bus, initially?

indicators.note: reduced means the rail-service word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a train is a rail service

indicators.note: catching means one word holds another letter inside it

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of bus

explanation.surface: A motorcycling fan, frustrated by a cut-back train service, takes the bus instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims TRAIN to TRAI; 'catching' puts B (first letter of 'bus') into LIKE to give LBIKE. A scramble is an off-road motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: A light motorcycle built for rough tracks is what riders use in a scramble, an off-road race.

clue.text: Where to eat bird's tail, popular covered with curry

indicators.note: a tail is the last part, so take the final letter of bird

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
in can mean wearing or covered, as in a man in a coat
to curry a horse is to groom it with a currycomb

explanation.surface: A recipe of bird served with a popular curry topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' is not food here: to curry a horse is to groom it. 'covered' gives a second IN, as in 'in a coat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A room set aside in a house for meals is the place where people eat.

clue.text: One admired public pool delaying its opening

indicators.note: delaying its opening means the first letter of the pool word is moved later, to the end

parts.note: a lido is a public open-air swimming pool

explanation.surface: Someone well liked at the local baths turns up late for the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delaying its opening' sends the L of LIDO (a British open-air public pool) to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worshipped or greatly looked up to is an object of admiration, like a pop star.

clue.text: Age badly after daughter, with regret over device for 28?

indicators.note: after means the age piece follows the daughter piece

parts.note: an era is an age
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Getting older poorly after having a daughter, with regrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses RUE to EUR. 28 is LANCE ARMSTRONG, the cyclist, so the device is part of a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The gear-changing mechanism on a racing bicycle shifts the chain between sprockets.

clue.text: Deliberate flick for hairstyle

parts.note: to deliberate is to mull something over
a flick is a film, and E.T. is Spielberg's famous one

explanation.surface: Thinking carefully before tossing one's hair with a flick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliberate' is a verb here, and 'flick' is slang for a film: E.T.
explanation.definitionFit: A haircut short at the front and long at the back is a well-known 1980s style.

clue.text: Wolf languishes, caged by priest and knight

indicators.note: caged by means the languish word is held inside the priest word

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
to languish is to fade away, and dies means fades
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A predatory beast wasting away in a cage kept by a priest and a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolf' looks like an animal but means a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser or seducer is a man who chases women, slang for a wolf.

clue.text: Sticking with manipulation one is had

indicators.note: manipulation means handling and reshaping, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A con trick in which the victim realises they have been fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with manipulation' rearranges ONEISHAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The property of clinging firmly to a surface is adherence, which is what sticking describes.

clue.text: Shut up shop, initially slicing cold loaf

indicators.note: slicing means a letter cuts into the loaf word

parts.note: to loaf is to loiter about idly

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of shop

explanation.surface: Closing the shop after cutting into a cold loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' is a verb here: to loiter. 'slicing' puts S (first of 'shop') inside LOITER.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine someone in seclusion, like a monk in a monastery, is to shut them away.

clue.text: Fool detaining duke's no upper-class Victorian rebel

indicators.note: detaining means the fool word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: nelly is British slang for a silly person

indicators.note: no upper-class means remove U, the standard abbreviation for upper-class

parts.note: duke as written, the possessive adding nothing

explanation.surface: A silly person holding a duke captive, a rebel of the Victorian era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no upper-class' drops U from the duke, and 'detaining' holds what is left inside the fool. 'Victorian' means from the Australian state of Victoria, not the era.
explanation.definitionFit: The notorious Australian bushranger who defied authorities in Victoria became a folk outlaw.

clue.text: Disconnect problem from emotional source

explanation.surface: Advice on ending a call that might be upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a phone call is to put down the receiver; a psychological complex or fixation is a neurotic issue.

clue.text: Female's superb settings for snapper

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, and the 's adds an S
tops is slang for excellent or the best

explanation.surface: A woman's excellent camera settings for a photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapper' is slang for a photographer, not the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Aperture stops on a camera lens are numbered settings a photographer chooses.

clue.text: Chunk of solid earth that's formed in the head?

indicators.note: Chunk of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lump of dry ground seems to have taken shape inside someone's skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought or notion is something the mind produces.

clue.text: Winslet not out of place here?

definitions.text: Winslet not out of place here?

indicators.note: out of place means the letters are moved from their positions and rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the actress Kate Winslet would fit in somewhere glamorous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' rearranges WINSLETNOT; the whole clue also defines, since a film star belongs in Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname for Hollywood, the film capital where stars like Kate Winslet work.

clue.text: Stars working round South American port

indicators.note: round means the working word goes around the port

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Celebrities working around a port in Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hunter is a bright constellation, a group of stars named for a mythic hunter.

clue.text: Time to split payment for gala

indicators.note: to split means the time letter breaks into the payment word

parts.note: a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: Time to share out the money raised at a summer gala.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival or outdoor celebration, often a village fundraiser, is a gala event.

clue.text: Wife in name -Eco's first helper

indicators.note: in means the wife letter goes inside the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: the Italian novelist Eco's first name was Umberto

explanation.surface: A spouse named in an Italian author's book, presented as his first assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eco's first' means the first name of Umberto Eco, author of The Name of the Rose; 'in' puts W inside N + UMBERTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy or second-in-command is an assistant to the leader.

clue.text: For cloth, there's no time at all to send away

indicators.note: there's no time at all means every T is removed from the cloth word

parts.note: a textile is a woven cloth

explanation.surface: No time to spare for fabric, so it gets sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no time at all' strips every T (time) from TEXTILE: both Ts go.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to force them out of their country.

clue.text: Jousting practice should make this champion rider

explanation.surface: A knight's training regime promises to produce a winning horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: Jousting practice should leave a lance arm strong; the champion rider is a cyclist, not a knight on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated tilting builds muscle in the limb holding the weapon; the American cyclist won the Tour de France repeatedly before being stripped of the titles.
